## The mvcgen tactic — 17.1. Overview {#manual-the-mvcgen-tactic-171-overview}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Overview/

The workflow of `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` consists of the following:

1. Monadic programs are re-interpreted according to a [predicate transformer semantics](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Predicate-Transformers/#--tech-term-predicate-transformer-semantics).
   An instance of `[WP](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Predicate-Transformers/#Std___Do___WP___mk)` determines the monad's interpretation.
   Each program is interpreted as a mapping from arbitrary [postconditions](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Predicate-Transformers/#--tech-term-postcondition) to the [weakest precondition](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Predicate-Transformers/#--tech-term-weakest-preconditions) that would ensure the postcondition.
   This step is invisible to most users, but library authors who want to enable their monads to work with `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` need to understand it.
2. Programs are composed from smaller programs.
   Each statement in a [`do`](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#Lean___Parser___Term___do)-block is associated with a predicate transformer, and there are general-purpose rules for combining these statements with sequencing and control-flow operators.
   A statement with its pre- and postconditions is called a [*Hoare triple*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Predicate-Transformers/#--tech-term-Hoare-triple).
   In a program, the postcondition of each statement should suffice to prove the precondition of the next one, and loops require a specified *loop invariant*, which is a statement that must be true at the beginning of the loop and at the end of each iteration.
   Designated [*specification lemmas*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Predicate-Transformers/#--tech-term-Specification-lemmas) associate functions with Hoare triples that specify them.
3. Applying the weakest-precondition semantics of a monadic program to a desired proof goal results in the precondition that must hold in order to prove the goal.
   Any missing steps such as loop invariants or proofs that a statement's precondition implies its postcondition become new subgoals.
   These missing steps are called the *verification conditions*.
   The `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` tactic performs this transformation, replacing the goal with its verification conditions.
   During this transformation, `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` uses specification lemmas to discharge proofs about individual statements.
4. After supplying loop invariants, many verification conditions can in practice be discharged automatically.
   Those that cannot can be proven using either a [special proof mode]](#manual-tactic-ref-spred) or ordinary Lean tactics, depending on whether they are expressed in the logic of program assertions or as ordinary propositions.

---



## The mvcgen tactic — 17.2. Predicate Transformers {#manual-the-mvcgen-tactic-172-predicate-transformers}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Predicate-Transformers/

A *predicate transformer semantics* is an interpretation of programs as functions from predicates to predicates, rather than values to values.
A *postcondition* is an assertion that holds after running a program, while a *precondition* is an assertion that must hold prior to running the program in order for the postcondition to be guaranteed to hold.

The predicate transformer semantics used by `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` transforms postconditions into the *weakest preconditions* under which the program will ensure the postcondition.
An assertion `P` is weaker than `P'` if, in all states, `P'` suffices to prove `P`, but `P` does not suffice to prove `P'`.
Logically equivalent assertions are considered to be equal.

The predicates in question are stateful: they can mention the program's current state.
Furthermore, postconditions can relate the return value and any exceptions thrown by the program to the final state.
`[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` is a type of predicates that is parameterized over a monadic state, expressed as a list of the types of the fields that make up the state.
The usual logical connectives and quantifiers are defined for `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`.
Each monad that can be used with `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` is assigned a state type by an instance of `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)`, and `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)` is the corresponding type of assertions for that monad, which is used for preconditions.
`[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)` is a wrapper around `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`: while `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` is parameterized by a list of states types, `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)` is parameterized by a more informative type that it translates to a list of state types for `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`.
A `[PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond)` pairs an `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)` about a return value with assertions about potential exceptions; the available exceptions are also specified by the monad's `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` instance.

### 17.2.1. Stateful Predicates {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Stateful-Predicates}

The predicate transformer semantics of monadic programs is based on a logic in which propositions may mention the program's state.
Here, “state” refers not only to mutable state, but also to read-only values such as those that are provided via `[ReaderT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#ReaderT)`.
Different monads have different state types available, but each individual state always has a type.
Given a list of state types, `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` is a type of predicates over these states.

`[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` is not inherently tied to the monadic verification framework.
The related `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)` computes a suitable `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` for a monad's state as expressed via its `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` instance's `[PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)` output parameter.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) (σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)) : Type u



[Std.Do.SPred.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) (σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)) :
  Type u
```

A predicate over states, where each state is defined by a list of component state types.

Example:

```lean
[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) [[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero), [Bool](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)] = ([Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Bool](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false) → [ULift]](#manual-ULift___up) Prop)
```

Ordinary propositions that do not mention the state can be used as stateful predicates by adding a trivial universal quantification.
This is written with the syntax `⌜P⌝`, which is syntactic sugar for `[SPred.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)`.

syntaxNotation for `SPred`

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ⌜term⌝
```

Embedding of pure Lean values into `[SVal]](#manual-Std___Do___SVal)`. An alias for `[SPred.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.pure.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P : Prop) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs



[Std.Do.SPred.pure.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)}
  (P : Prop) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs
```

A pure proposition `P : Prop` embedded into `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`.
Prefer to use notation `⌜P⌝`.

**Example: Stateful Predicates**

The predicate `[ItIsSecret]](#manual-ItIsSecret-_LPAR_in-Stateful-Predicates_RPAR_)` expresses that a state of type `[String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)` is `"secret"`:

```lean
def ItIsSecret : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) [[String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)] := fun s => ⌜s = "secret"⌝
```

#### 17.2.1.1. Entailment {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Stateful-Predicates--Entailment}

Stateful predicates are related by *entailment*.
Entailment of stateful predicates is defined as universally-quantified implication: if `P` and `Q` are predicates over a state `\sigma`, then `P` entails `Q` (written `P \vdash_s Q`) when `∀ s : \sigma, P(s) → Q(s)`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.entails.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___entails) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : Prop



[Std.Do.SPred.entails.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___entails)
  {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) :
  Prop
```

Entailment in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`.

One predicate `P` entails another predicate `Q` if `Q` is true in every state in which `P` is true.
Unlike implication (`[SPred.imp]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___imp)`), entailment is not itself an `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`, but is instead an ordinary
proposition.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.bientails.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___bientails) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : Prop



[Std.Do.SPred.bientails.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___bientails)
  {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) :
  Prop
```

Logical equivalence of `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`.

Logically equivalent predicates are equal. Use `SPred.bientails.to_eq` to convert bi-entailment to
equality.

syntaxNotation for `SPred`

```lean
term ::= ...
    | term ⊢ₛ term
```

Entailment in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`; sugar for `[SPred.entails]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___entails)`.

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ⊢ₛ term
```

Tautology in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`; sugar for `[SPred.entails]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___entails) ⌜[True](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Truth/#True___intro)⌝`.

```lean
term ::= ...
    | term ⊣⊢ₛ term
```

Bi-entailment in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`; sugar for `[SPred.bientails]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___bientails)`.

The logic of stateful predicates includes an implication connective.
The difference between entailment and implication is that entailment is a statement in Lean's logic, while implication is internal to the stateful logic.
Given stateful predicates `P` and `Q` for state `σ`, `P ⊢ₛ Q` is a `Prop` while `spred(P → Q)` is an `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σ`.

#### 17.2.1.2. Notation {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Stateful-Predicates--Notation}

The syntax of stateful predicates overlaps with that of ordinary Lean terms.
In particular, stateful predicates use the usual syntax for logical connectives and quantifiers.
The syntax associated with stateful predicates is automatically enabled in contexts such as pre- and postconditions where they are clearly intended; other contexts must explicitly opt in to the syntax using `spred`.
The usual meanings of these operators can be recovered by using the [`term`]](#manual-Std___Do____FLQQ_termTerm_LPAR___RPAR__FLQQ_) operator.

syntaxPredicate Terms

`spred` indicates that logical connectives and quantifiers should be understood as those pertaining to stateful predicates, while [`term`]](#manual-Std___Do____FLQQ_termTerm_LPAR___RPAR__FLQQ_) indicates that they should have the usual meaning.

```lean
term ::= ...
    | spred(term)
```

```lean
term ::= ...
    | term(term)
```

#### 17.2.1.3. Connectives and Quantifiers {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Stateful-Predicates--Connectives-and-Quantifiers}

syntaxPredicate Connectives


def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.and.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___and) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs



[Std.Do.SPred.and.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___and) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)}
  (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs
```

Conjunction in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`: states that satisfy `P` and satisfy `Q` satisfy `spred(P ∧ Q)`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.conjunction.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___conjunction) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)}
  (env : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) ([SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs)) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs



[Std.Do.SPred.conjunction.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___conjunction)
  {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)}
  (env : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) ([SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs)) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs
```

Conjunction of a list of stateful predicates. A state satisfies `conjunction env` if it satisfies
all predicates in `env`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.or.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___or) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs



[Std.Do.SPred.or.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___or) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)}
  (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs
```

Disjunction in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`: states that either satisfy `P` or satisfy `Q` satisfy `spred(P ∨ Q)`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.not.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___not) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs



[Std.Do.SPred.not.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___not) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)}
  (P : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs
```

Negation in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`: states that do not satisfy `P` satisfy `spred(¬ P)`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.imp.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___imp) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs



[Std.Do.SPred.imp.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___imp) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)}
  (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs
```

Implication in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`: states that satisfy `Q` whenever they satisfy `P` satisfy `spred(P → Q)`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.iff.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___iff) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)} (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs



[Std.Do.SPred.iff.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___iff) {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)}
  (P Q : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs
```

Biimplication in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`: states that either satisfy both `P` and `Q` or satisfy neither satisfy
`spred(P ↔ Q)`.

```lean
    | spred(∀ ([_]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Term___hole) (ident | [hole]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Term___hole))* : term),  term)
```

Each form of universal quantification is syntactic sugar for an invocation of `[SPred.forall]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___forall)` on a function that takes the quantified variable as a parameter.

```lean
term ::= ...
    | spred(∃ ident, term)
```

```lean
term ::= ...
    | spred(∃ ident : term,  term)
```

```lean
term ::= ...
    | spred(∃ (ident binderIdent* : term),  term)
```

```lean
term ::= ...
    | spred(∃ [_]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Term___hole), term)
```

```lean
term ::= ...
    | spred(∃ [_]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Term___hole) : term,  term)
```

```lean
term ::= ...
    | spred(∃ ([_]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Term___hole) binderIdent* : term),  term)
```

Each form of existential quantification is syntactic sugar for an invocation of `[SPred.exists]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___exists)` on a function that takes the quantified variable as a parameter.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.SPred.forall.{u, v}]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___forall) {α : Sort u} {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type v)}
  (P : α → [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs

  {σs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type v)}
  (P : α → [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs) : [SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) σs
```

Universal quantifier in `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`.

def


### 17.2.2. Assertions {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Assertions}

The language of assertions about monadic programs is parameterized by a *postcondition shape*, which describes the inputs to and outputs from a computation in a given monad.
Preconditions may mention the initial values of the monad's state, while postconditions may mention the returned value, the final values of the monad's state, and must furthermore account for any exceptions that could have been thrown.
The postcondition shape of a given monad determines the states and exceptions in the monad.
`[PostShape.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)` describes a monad in which assertions may not mention any states, `[PostShape.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)` describes a state value, and `[PostShape.except]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)` describes a possible exception.
Because these constructors can be continually added, the postcondition shape of a monad transformer can be defined in terms of the postcondition shape of the underlying transformed monad.
Behind the scenes, an `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)` is translated into an appropriate `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` by translating the postcondition shape into a list of state types, discarding exceptions.

inductive type

```lean
[Std.Do.PostShape.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) : Type (u + 1)



[Std.Do.PostShape.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) : Type (u + 1)
```

The “shape” of the postconditions that are used to reason about a monad.

A postcondition shape is an abstraction of many possible monadic effects, based on the structure of pure functions that can simulate them. The postcondition shape of a monad is given by its `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` instance. This shape is used to determine both its `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)`s and its `[PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond)`s.

Constructors

```lean
[Std.Do.PostShape.pure.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)
```

The assertions and postconditions in this monad use neither state nor exceptions.

```lean
[Std.Do.PostShape.arg.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) (σ : Type u) :
  [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) → [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)
```

The assertions in this monad may mention the current value of a state of type `σ`, and
postconditions may mention the state's final value.

```lean
[Std.Do.PostShape.except.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) (ε : Type u) :
  [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) → [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)
```

The postconditions in this monad include assertions about exceptional values of type `ε` that
result from premature termination.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PostShape.args.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___args) : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) → [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)



[Std.Do.PostShape.args.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___args) :
  [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) → [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) (Type u)
```

Extracts the list of state types under `[PostShape.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)` constructors, discarding exception types.

The state types determine the shape of assertions in the monad.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.Assertion.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) (ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) : Type u



[Std.Do.Assertion.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) (ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) :
  Type u
```

An assertion about the state fields for a monad whose postcondition shape is `ps`.

Concretely, this is an abbreviation for `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` applied to the `.arg`s in the given predicate shape, so all theorems about `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` apply.

Examples:

```
example : Assertion (.arg ρ .pure) = (ρ → ULift Prop) := rfl
example : Assertion (.except ε .pure) = ULift Prop := rfl
example : Assertion (.arg σ (.except ε .pure)) = (σ → ULift Prop) := rfl
example : Assertion (.except ε (.arg σ .pure)) = (σ → ULift Prop) := rfl
```

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PostCond.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) (α : Type u) (ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) : Type u



[Std.Do.PostCond.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) (α : Type u)
  (ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) : Type u
```

A postcondition for the given predicate shape, with one `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)` for the terminating case and
one `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion)` for each `.except` layer in the predicate shape.

```
variable (α σ ε : Type)
example : PostCond α (.arg σ .pure) = ((α → σ → ULift Prop) × PUnit) := rfl
example : PostCond α (.except ε .pure) = ((α → ULift Prop) × (ε → ULift Prop) × PUnit) := rfl
example : PostCond α (.arg σ (.except ε .pure)) = ((α → σ → ULift Prop) × (ε → ULift Prop) × PUnit) := rfl
example : PostCond α (.except ε (.arg σ .pure)) = ((α → σ → ULift Prop) × (ε → σ → ULift Prop) × PUnit) := rfl
```

syntaxPostconditions

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ⇓ term* => term
```

Syntactic sugar for a nested sequence of product constructors, terminating in `()`, in which the first element is an assertion about non-exceptional return values and the remaining elements are assertions about the exceptional cases for a postcondition.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.ExceptConds.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___ExceptConds) : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) → Type u



[Std.Do.ExceptConds.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___ExceptConds) :
  [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) → Type u
```

An assertion about each potential exception that's declared in a postcondition shape.

Examples:

```
example : ExceptConds (.pure) = Unit := rfl
example : ExceptConds (.except ε .pure) = ((ε → ULift Prop) × Unit) := rfl
example : ExceptConds (.arg σ (.except ε .pure)) = ((ε → ULift Prop) × Unit) := rfl
example : ExceptConds (.except ε (.arg σ .pure)) = ((ε → σ → ULift Prop) × Unit) := rfl
```

Postconditions for programs that might throw exceptions come in two varieties. The *total correctness interpretation* `⦃P⦄ prog ⦃⇓ r => Q' r⦄` asserts that, given `P` holds, then `prog` terminates *and* `Q'` holds for the result. The *partial correctness interpretation* `⦃P⦄ prog ⦃⇓? r => Q' r⦄` asserts that, given `P` holds, and *if* `prog` terminates *then* `Q'` holds for the result.

syntaxException-Free Postconditions

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ⇓ term* => term
```

A postcondition expressing total correctness.
That is, it expresses that the asserted computation finishes without throwing an exception
*and* the result satisfies the given predicate `p`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PostCond.noThrow.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___noThrow) {α : Type u_1} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  (p : α → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps



[Std.Do.PostCond.noThrow.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___noThrow)
  {α : Type u_1} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  (p : α → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps
```

A postcondition expressing total correctness.
That is, it expresses that the asserted computation finishes without throwing an exception
*and* the result satisfies the given predicate `p`.

syntaxPartial Postconditions

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ⇓? term* => term
```

A postcondition expressing partial correctness.
That is, it expresses that *if* the asserted computation finishes without throwing an exception
*then* the result satisfies the given predicate `p`.
Nothing is asserted when the computation throws an exception.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PostCond.mayThrow.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___mayThrow) {α : Type u_1} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  (p : α → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps



[Std.Do.PostCond.mayThrow.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___mayThrow)
  {α : Type u_1} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  (p : α → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps
```

A postcondition expressing partial correctness.
That is, it expresses that *if* the asserted computation finishes without throwing an exception
*then* the result satisfies the given predicate `p`.
Nothing is asserted when the computation throws an exception.

syntaxPostcondition Entailment

```lean
term ::= ...
    | term ⊢ₚ term
```

Syntactic sugar for `[PostCond.entails]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___entails)`

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PostCond.entails.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___entails) {α : Type u_1} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  (p q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps) : Prop



[Std.Do.PostCond.entails.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___entails)
  {α : Type u_1} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  (p q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps) : Prop
```

Entailment of postconditions.

This consists of:

- Entailment of the assertion about the return value, for all possible return values.
- Entailment of the exception conditions.

While implication of postconditions (`[PostCond.imp]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___imp)`) results in a new postcondition, entailment is
an ordinary proposition.

syntaxPostcondition Conjunction

```lean
term ::= ...
    | term ∧ₚ term
```

Syntactic sugar for `[PostCond.and]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___and)`

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PostCond.and.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___and) {α : Type u_1} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  (p q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps) : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps



[Std.Do.PostCond.and.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___and) {α : Type u_1}
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} (p q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps) :
  [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps
```

Conjunction of postconditions.

This is defined pointwise, as the conjunction of the assertions about the return value and the
conjunctions of the assertions about each potential exception.

syntaxPostcondition Implication

```lean
term ::= ...
    | term →ₚ term
```

Syntactic sugar for `[PostCond.imp]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___imp)`

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PostCond.imp.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___imp) {α : Type u_1} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  (p q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps) : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps



[Std.Do.PostCond.imp.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___imp) {α : Type u_1}
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} (p q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps) :
  [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps
```

Implication of postconditions.

This is defined pointwise, as the implication of the assertions about the return value and the
implications of each of the assertions about each potential exception.

While entailment of postconditions (`[PostCond.entails]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___entails)`) is an ordinary proposition, implication of
postconditions is itself a postcondition.

### 17.2.3. Predicate Transformers {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Predicate-Transformers}

A predicate transformer is a function from postconditions for some postcondition state into assertions for that state.
The function must be *conjunctive*, which means it must distribute over `[PostCond.and]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___and)`.

structure

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) (ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) (α : Type u) : Type u



[Std.Do.PredTrans.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) (ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure))
  (α : Type u) : Type u
```

The type of predicate transformers for a given `ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)` and return type `α : Type`. A
predicate transformer `x : [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps α` is a function that takes a postcondition `Q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps` and returns a precondition `x.apply Q : [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps`.

Constructor

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.mk]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk).{u}
```

Fields

```lean
trans : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps
```

The function implementing the predicate transformer.

```lean
conjunctiveRaw : [PredTrans.Conjunctive]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___Conjunctive) self.[trans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk)
```

The predicate transformer is conjunctive: `t (Q₁ ∧ₚ Q₂) ⊣⊢ₛ t Q₁ ∧ t Q₂`.
So the stronger the postcondition, the stronger the resulting precondition.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.Conjunctive.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___Conjunctive) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α : Type u}
  (t : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) : Prop



[Std.Do.PredTrans.Conjunctive.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___Conjunctive)
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α : Type u}
  (t : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) :
  Prop
```

Transforming a conjunction of postconditions is the same as the conjunction of transformed
postconditions.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.Monotonic.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___Monotonic) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α : Type u}
  (t : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) : Prop



[Std.Do.PredTrans.Monotonic.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___Monotonic)
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α : Type u}
  (t : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) :
  Prop
```

The stronger the postcondition, the stronger the transformed precondition.

Predicate transformers form a monad.
The `[pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk)` operator is the identity transformer; it simply instantiates the postcondition with the its argument.
The `[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk)` operator composes predicate transformers.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.pure.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pure) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α : Type u} (a : α) :
  [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps α



[Std.Do.PredTrans.pure.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pure) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  {α : Type u} (a : α) : [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps α
```

The identity predicate transformer that transforms the postcondition's assertion about the return
value into an assertion about `a`.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.bind.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___bind) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α β : Type u}
  (x : [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps α) (f : α → [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps β) : [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps β



[Std.Do.PredTrans.bind.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___bind) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  {α β : Type u} (x : [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps α)
  (f : α → [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps β) :
  [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps β
```

Sequences two predicate transformers by composing them.

The helper operators `[PredTrans.pushArg]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushArg)`, `[PredTrans.pushExcept]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushExcept)`, and `[PredTrans.pushOption]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushOption)` modify a predicate transformer by adding a standard side effect.
They are used to implement the `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` instances for transformers such as `[StateT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateT)`, `[ExceptT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#ExceptT)`, and `[OptionT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#OptionT)`; they can also be used to implement monads that can be thought of in terms of one of these.
For example, `[PredTrans.pushArg]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushArg)` is typically used for state monads, but can also be used to implement a reader monad's instance, treating the reader's value as read-only state.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.pushArg.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushArg) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α σ : Type u}
  (x : [StateT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateT) σ ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α) : [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([PostShape.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) σ ps) α



[Std.Do.PredTrans.pushArg.{u}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushArg)
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α σ : Type u}
  (x : [StateT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateT) σ ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α) :
  [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([PostShape.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) σ ps) α
```

Adds the ability to make assertions about a state of type `σ` to a predicate transformer with
postcondition shape `ps`, resulting in postcondition shape `.arg σ ps`. This is done by
interpreting `[StateT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateT) σ ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α` into `[PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) σ ps) α`.

This can be used to for all kinds of state-like effects, including reader effects or append-only
states, by interpreting them as states.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.pushExcept.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushExcept) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α ε : Type u_1}
  (x : [ExceptT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#ExceptT) ε ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α) : [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([PostShape.except]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) ε ps) α



[Std.Do.PredTrans.pushExcept.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushExcept)
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α ε : Type u_1}
  (x : [ExceptT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#ExceptT) ε ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α) :
  [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([PostShape.except]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) ε ps) α
```

Adds the ability to make assertions about exceptions of type `ε` to a predicate transformer with
postcondition shape `ps`, resulting in postcondition shape `.except ε ps`. This is done by
interpreting `[ExceptT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#ExceptT) ε ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α` into `[PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([.except]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) ε ps) α`.

This can be used for all kinds of exception-like effects, such as early termination, by interpreting
them as exceptions.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.PredTrans.pushOption.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushOption) {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α : Type u_1}
  (x : [OptionT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#OptionT) ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α) :
  [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([PostShape.except]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) [PUnit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#PUnit___unit) ps) α



[Std.Do.PredTrans.pushOption.{u_1}]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushOption)
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α : Type u_1}
  (x : [OptionT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#OptionT) ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α) :
  [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([PostShape.except]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) [PUnit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#PUnit___unit) ps) α
```

Adds the ability to make assertions about early termination to a predicate transformer with
postcondition shape `ps`, resulting in postcondition shape `.except PUnit ps`. This is done by
interpreting `[OptionT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#OptionT) ([PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps) α` into `[PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ([.except]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) [PUnit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#PUnit___unit) ps) α`, which models the type
`[Option](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Optional-Values/#Option___none)` as being equivalent to `[Except](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#Except___error) [PUnit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#PUnit___unit)`.

#### 17.2.3.1. Weakest Preconditions {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Predicate-Transformers--Weakest-Preconditions}

The [weakest precondition]](#manual---tech-term-weakest-preconditions) semantics of a monad are provided by the `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` type class.
Instances of `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` determine the monad's postcondition shape and provide the logical rules for interpreting the monad's operations as a predicate transformer in its postcondition shape.

type class

```lean
[Std.Do.WP.{u, v}]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk) (m : Type u → Type v) (ps : [outParam]](#manual-outParam) [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) :
  Type (max (u + 1) v)



[Std.Do.WP.{u, v}]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk) (m : Type u → Type v)
  (ps : [outParam]](#manual-outParam) [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) :
  Type (max (u + 1) v)
```

A weakest precondition interpretation of a monadic program `x : m α` in terms of a predicate
transformer `[PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps α`. The monad `m` determines `ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)`.

For practical reasoning, an instance of `[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk) m ps` is typically needed in addition to `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk) m ps`.

Instance Constructor

```lean
[Std.Do.WP.mk]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk).{u, v}
```

Methods

```lean
wp : {α : Type u} → m α → [PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps α
```

Interpret a monadic program `x : m α` in terms of a predicate transformer `[PredTrans]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___mk) ps α`.

syntaxWeakest Preconditions

```lean
term ::= ...
    | wp⟦term (: term)?⟧
```

`wp⟦x⟧ Q` is defined as `(WP.wp x).apply Q`.

#### 17.2.3.2. Weakest Precondition Monad Morphisms {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Predicate-Transformers--Weakest-Precondition-Monad-Morphisms}

Most of the built-in specification lemmas for `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` relies on the presence of a `[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk)` instance, in addition to the `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` instance.
In addition to being lawful, weakest preconditions of the monad's implementations of `[pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk)` and `[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk)` should correspond to the `[pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk)` and `[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk)` operators for the predicate transformer monad.
Without a `[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk)` instance, `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` typically returns the original proof goal unchanged.

type class

```lean
[Std.Do.WPMonad.{u, v}]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk) (m : Type u → Type v) (ps : [outParam]](#manual-outParam) [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure))
  [[Monad](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Monad___mk) m] : Type (max (u + 1) v)



[Std.Do.WPMonad.{u, v}]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk)
  (m : Type u → Type v)
  (ps : [outParam]](#manual-outParam) [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) [[Monad](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Monad___mk) m] :
  Type (max (u + 1) v)
```

A monad with weakest preconditions (`[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)`) that is also a monad morphism, preserving `[pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk)` and
`[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk)`.

In practice, `mvcgen` is not useful for reasoning about programs in a monad that is without a
`[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk)` instance. The specification lemmas for `[Pure.pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk)` and `[Bind.bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk)`, as well as those for
operators like `[Functor.map](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Functor___mk)`, require that their monad have a `[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk)` instance.

Instance Constructor

```lean
[Std.Do.WPMonad.mk]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk).{u, v}
```

Extends

- `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk) m ps`

**Example: Missing WPMonad Instance**

The single-field structure `[Identity]](#manual-Identity-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_)` acts like the identity monad `[Id](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#Id)`. It has a `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` instance, but no `[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk)` instance:

```lean
structure Identity (α : Type u) where
run : α
[variable]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___variable) {α : Type u}
instance : [Monad](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Monad___mk) [Identity]](#manual-Identity-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_) where
[pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk) x := ⟨x⟩
[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk) x f := f x.[run]](#manual-Identity___run-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_)
instance : [WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk) [Identity]](#manual-Identity-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_) [.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) where
[wp]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk) x := [PredTrans.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pure) x.[run]](#manual-Identity___run-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_)
theorem Identity.of_wp_run_eq {x : α} {prog : [Identity]](#manual-Identity-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_) α}
(h : [Identity.run]](#manual-Identity___run-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_) prog = x) (P : α → Prop) :
(⊢ₛ wp⟦prog⟧ (⇓ a => ⟨P a⟩)) → P x := byα:Type ux:αprog:[Identity]](#manual-Identity-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_) αh:prog.[run]](#manual-Identity___run-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_) [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) xP:α → Prop⊢ [(]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___entails)[⊢ₛ]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___entails) wp⟦prog⟧ ([PostCond.noThrow]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___noThrow) fun a => [{]](#manual-ULift___up) [down]](#manual-ULift___up) [:=]](#manual-ULift___up) P a [}]](#manual-ULift___up))[)]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___entails) → P x
[simp_all]](#manual-simp_all) [[WP.wp]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk), ← h]All goals completed! 🐙
```

The missing instance prevents `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` from using its specifications for `[pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk)` and `[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk)`.
This tends to show up as a verification condition that's equal to the original goal.
This function that reverses a list:

```lean
def rev (xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) : [Identity]](#manual-Identity-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_) ([List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) := [do](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#Lean___Parser___Term___do)
let mut out := []
for x in xs do
out := x :: out
return out
```

It is correct if it is equal to `[List.reverse](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___reverse)`.

When the verification condition is just the original problem, without even any simplification of `[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk)`, the problem is usually a missing `[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk)` instance.
The issue can be resolved by adding a suitable instance:

```lean
instance : [WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk) [Identity]](#manual-Identity-_LPAR_in-Missing--WPMonad--Instance_RPAR_) [.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) where
wp_pure _ := [rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#rfl-next)
wp_bind _ _ := [rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#rfl-next)
```

#### 17.2.3.3. Adequacy Lemmas {#manual-mvcgen-adequacy}

Monads that can be invoked from pure code typically provide a invocation operator that takes any required input state as a parameter and returns either a value paired with an output state or some kind of exceptional value.
Examples include `[StateT.run](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateT___run)`, `[ExceptT.run](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#ExceptT___run)`, and `[Id.run](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#Id___run)`.
*Adequacy lemmas* provide a bridge between statements about invocations of monadic programs and those programs' [weakest precondition]](#manual---tech-term-weakest-preconditions) semantics as given by their `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` instances.
They show that a property about the invocation is true if its weakest precondition is true.

### 17.2.4. Hoare Triples {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Hoare-Triples}

A *Hoare triple* (Hoare, 1969)C. A. R. Hoare (1969). “An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming”. *Communications of the ACM.* **12**(10), pp. 576–583. consists of a precondition, a program, and a postcondition.
Running the program in a state for which the precondition is true results in a state where the postcondition is true.

def

```lean

  {α : Type u} (x : m α) (P : [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps) (Q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps) : Prop



[Std.Do.Triple.{u, v}]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) {m : Type u → Type v}
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} [[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk) m ps] {α : Type u}
  (x : m α) (P : [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps)
  (Q : [PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) α ps) : Prop
```

A Hoare triple for reasoning about monadic programs. A Hoare triple `[Triple]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) x P Q` is a
*specification* for `x`: if assertion `P` holds before `x`, then postcondition `Q` holds after
running `x`.

`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is convenient syntax for `[Triple]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) x P Q`.

syntaxHoare Triples

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ⦃ term ⦄ term ⦃ term ⦄
```

`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is syntactic sugar for `[Triple]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) x P Q`.

Modus ponens for two Hoare triple specifications of a program `x`.
This theorem is useful for separating proofs. If `h₁ : [Triple]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) x P₁ Q₁` proves a basic property about
`x` and `h₂ : [Triple]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) x P₂ (Q₁ →ₚ Q₂)` is an advanced proof for `Q₂` that builds on the basic proof
for `Q₁`, then `mp x h₁ h₂` is a proof for `Q₂` about `x`.

### 17.2.5. Specification Lemmas {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Specification-Lemmas}

*Specification lemmas* are designated theorems that associate Hoare triples with functions.
When `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` encounters a function, it checks whether there are any registered specification lemmas and attempts to use them to discharge intermediate [verification conditions]](#manual---tech-term-verification-conditions).
If there is no applicable specification lemma, then the connection between the statement's pre- and postconditions will become a verification condition.
Specification lemmas allow compositional reasoning about libraries of monadic code.

When applied to a theorem whose statement is a Hoare triple, the `spec` attribute registers the theorem as a specification lemma.
These lemmas are used in order of priority.

The `spec` attribute may also be applied to definitions.
On definitions, it indicates that the definition should be unfolded during verification condition generation.

attributeSpecification Lemmas

```lean
attr ::= ...
    | spec prio?
```

Theorems tagged with the `[spec]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Attr___spec)` attribute are used by the `mspec` and `mvcgen` tactics.

- When used on a theorem `foo_spec : Triple (foo a b c) P Q`, then `mspec` and `mvcgen` will use
  `foo_spec` as a specification for calls to `foo`.
- Otherwise, when used on a definition that `@[simp]` would work on, it is added to the internal
  simp set of `mvcgen` that is used within `wp⟦·⟧` contexts to simplify match discriminants and
  applications of constants.

Universally-quantified variables in specification lemmas can be used to relate input states to output states and return values.
These variables are referred to as *schematic variables*.

**Example: Schematic Variables**

The function `[double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Variables_RPAR_)` doubles the value of a `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)` state:

```lean
def double : [StateM](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateM) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) [Unit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#Unit) := [do](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#Lean___Parser___Term___do)
[modify](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#modify) (2 * ·)
```

Its specification should *relate* the initial and final states, but it cannot know their precise values.
The specification uses a schematic variable to stand for the initial state:

```lean
theorem double_spec :
⦃ fun s => ⌜s = n⌝ ⦄ [double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Variables_RPAR_) ⦃ ⇓ () s => ⌜s = 2 * n⌝ ⦄ := byn:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[fun]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) s [=>]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) n[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Variables_RPAR_) [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[PostCond.noThrow]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___noThrow) fun x s => [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 2 [*]](#manual-HMul___mk) n[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)
[simp]](#manual-simp) [[double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Variables_RPAR_)]n:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[fun]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) s [=>]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) n[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [modify](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#modify) fun x => 2 [*]](#manual-HMul___mk) x [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[PostCond.noThrow]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___noThrow) fun x s => [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 2 [*]](#manual-HMul___mk) n[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)
mvcgen with [grind]](#manual-grind)All goals completed! 🐙
```

The assertion in the precondition is a function because the `[PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)` of `[StateM](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateM) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)` is `[.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) [.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)`, and `[Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ([.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) [.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure))` is `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred) [[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)]`.

### 17.2.6. Invariant Specifications {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--The--mvcgen--tactic--Predicate-Transformers--Invariant-Specifications}

These types are used in invariants.
The [specification lemmas]](#manual---tech-term-Specification-lemmas) for `[ForIn.forIn](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#ForIn___mk)` and `[ForIn'.forIn'](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#ForIn______mk)` take parameters of type `[Invariant]](#manual-Std___Do___Invariant)`, and `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` ensures that invariants are not accidentally generated by other automation.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.Invariant.{u₁, u₂}]](#manual-Std___Do___Invariant) {α : Type u₁} (xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) (β : Type u₂)
  (ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) : Type (max u₂ u₁)



[Std.Do.Invariant.{u₁, u₂}]](#manual-Std___Do___Invariant) {α : Type u₁}
  (xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) (β : Type u₂)
  (ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) : Type (max u₂ u₁)
```

The type of loop invariants used by the specifications of `for ... in ...` loops.
A loop invariant is a `[PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond)` that takes as parameters

- A `[List.Cursor]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk) xs` representing the iteration state of the loop. It is parameterized by the list
  of elements `xs` that the `for` loop iterates over.
- A state tuple of type `β`, which will be a nesting of `[MProd](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#MProd___mk)`s representing the elaboration of
  `let mut` variables and early return.

The loop specification lemmas will use this in the following way:
Before entering the loop, the cursor's prefix is empty and the suffix is `xs`.
After leaving the loop, the cursor's prefix is `xs` and the suffix is empty.
During the induction step, the invariant holds for a suffix with head element `x`.
After running the loop body, the invariant then holds after shifting `x` to the prefix.

def

```lean
[Std.Do.Invariant.withEarlyReturn.{u₁, u₂}]](#manual-Std___Do___Invariant___withEarlyReturn) {β : Type (max u₁ u₂)}
  {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)} {α : Type (max u₁ u₂)} {xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α}
  {γ : Type (max u₁ u₂)} (onContinue : xs.[Cursor]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk) → β → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps)
  (onReturn : γ → β → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps)
  (onExcept : [ExceptConds]](#manual-Std___Do___ExceptConds) ps := ExceptConds.false) :
  [Invariant]](#manual-Std___Do___Invariant) xs ([MProd](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#MProd___mk) ([Option](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Optional-Values/#Option___none) γ) β) ps



[Std.Do.Invariant.withEarlyReturn.{u₁, u₂}]](#manual-Std___Do___Invariant___withEarlyReturn)
  {β : Type (max u₁ u₂)} {ps : [PostShape]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)}
  {α : Type (max u₁ u₂)} {xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α}
  {γ : Type (max u₁ u₂)}
  (onContinue :
    xs.[Cursor]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk) → β → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps)
  (onReturn : γ → β → [Assertion]](#manual-Std___Do___Assertion) ps)
  (onExcept : [ExceptConds]](#manual-Std___Do___ExceptConds) ps :=
    ExceptConds.false) :
  [Invariant]](#manual-Std___Do___Invariant) xs ([MProd](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#MProd___mk) ([Option](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Optional-Values/#Option___none) γ) β) ps
```

Helper definition for specifying loop invariants for loops with early return.

`for ... in ...` loops with early return of type `γ` elaborate to a call like this:

```
forIn (β := MProd (Option γ) ...) (b := ⟨none, ...⟩) collection loopBody
```

Note that the first component of the `[MProd](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#MProd___mk)` state tuple is the optional early return value.
It is `[none](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Optional-Values/#Option___none)` as long as there was no early return and `[some](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Optional-Values/#Option___none) r` if the loop returned early with `r`.

This function allows to specify different invariants for the loop body depending on whether the loop
terminated early or not. When there was an early return, the loop has effectively finished, which is
encoded by the additional `⌜xs.suffix = []⌝` assertion in the invariant. This assertion is vital for
successfully proving the induction step, as it contradicts with the assumption that
`xs.suffix = x::rest` of the inductive hypothesis at the start of the loop body, meaning that users
won't need to prove anything about the bogus case where the loop has returned early yet takes
another iteration of the loop body.

Invariants use lists to model the sequence of values in a `for` loop.
The current position in the loop is tracked with a `[List.Cursor]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk)` that represents a position in a list as a combination of the elements to the left of the position and the elements to the right.
This type is not a traditional zipper, in which the prefix is reversed for efficient movement: it is intended for use in specifications and proofs, not in run-time code, so the prefix is in the original order.

structure

```lean
[List.Cursor.{u}]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk) {α : Type u} (l : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) : Type u



[List.Cursor.{u}]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk) {α : Type u}
  (l : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) : Type u
```

A pointer at a specific location in a list. List cursors are used in loop invariants for the
`mvcgen` tactic.

Moving the cursor to the left or right takes time linear in the current position of the cursor, so
this data structure is not appropriate for run-time code.

Constructor

```lean
[List.Cursor.mk]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk).{u}
```

Fields

```lean
prefix : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α
```

The elements before to the current position in the list.

```lean
suffix : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α
```

The elements starting at the current position. If the position is after the last element of the
list, then the suffix is empty; otherwise, the first element of the suffix is the current element
that the cursor points to.

```lean
property : self.[prefix]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk) [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) self.[suffix]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk) [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) l
```

Appending the prefix to the suffix yields the original list.

def

```lean
[List.Cursor.at.{u_1}]](#manual-List___Cursor___at) {α : Type u_1} (l : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : l.[Cursor]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk)



[List.Cursor.at.{u_1}]](#manual-List___Cursor___at) {α : Type u_1}
  (l : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : l.[Cursor]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk)
```

Creates a cursor at position `n` in the list `l`.
The prefix contains the first `n` elements, and the suffix contains the remaining elements.
If `n` is larger than the length of the list, the cursor is positioned at the end of the list.

```lean
[List.Cursor.pos.{u_1}]](#manual-List___Cursor___pos) {α✝ : Type u_1}
  {l : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α✝} (c : l.[Cursor]](#manual-List___Cursor___mk)) : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
```

The position of the cursor in the list.

Requires that is a current element: the suffix must be non-empty, so the cursor is not at the end of

## The mvcgen tactic — 17.3. Verification Conditions {#manual-the-mvcgen-tactic-173-verification-conditions}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Verification-Conditions/

The `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` tactic converts a goal that's expressed in terms of `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)` and weakest preconditions to a set of invariants and verification conditions that, together, suffice to prove the original goal.
In particular, [Hoare triples]](#manual---tech-term-Hoare-triple) are defined in terms of weakest preconditions, so `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` can be used to prove them.

The verification conditions for a goal are generated as follows:

1. A number of simplifications and rewrites are applied.
2. The goal should now be of the form `P ⊢ₛ wp⟦e⟧ Q` (that is, an entailment from some set of stateful assumptions to the weakest precondition that implies a desired postcondition).
3. [Reducible]](#manual---tech-term-Reducible) constants and definitions marked `[@[]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Term___attributes-next)spec[]](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Attributes/#Lean___Parser___Term___attributes-next)` in the expression `e` are unfolded.
4. If the expression is an application of an [auxiliary matching function]](#manual---tech-term-auxiliary-matching-functions) or a conditional (`ite` or `dite`), then it is first simplified.
   The [discriminant]](#manual---tech-term-match-discriminants) of each matcher is simplified, and the entire term is reduced in an attempt to eliminate the matcher or conditional.
   If this fails, then a new goal is generated for each branch.
5. If the expression is an application of a constant, then the applicable lemmas marked `[@[]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Term___attributes-next)spec[]](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Attributes/#Lean___Parser___Term___attributes-next)` are attempted in priority order.
   Lean includes specification lemmas for constants such as `[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk)`, `[pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk)`, and `[ForIn.forIn](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#ForIn___mk)` that result from desugaring [`do`](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#Lean___Parser___Term___do)-notation.
   Instantiating the lemma will sometimes discharge its premises, in particular schematic variables due to definitional equalities with the goal.
   Assumptions of type `[Invariant]](#manual-Std___Do___Invariant)` are never instantiated this way, however.
   If the spec lemma's precondition or postcondition do not exactly match those of the goal, then new metavariables are created that prove the necessary entailments.
   If these cannot be immediately discharged using simple automation that attempts to use local assumptions and decomposes conjunctions in postconditions, then they remain as verification conditions.
6. Each remaining goal created by this process is recursively processed for verification conditions if it has the form `P ⊢ₛ wp⟦e⟧ Q`. If not, it is added to the set of invariants or verification conditions.
7. The resulting subgoals for invariants and verification conditions are assigned suitable names in the proof state.
8. Depending on the tactic's configuration parameters, `mvcgen_trivial` and `[mleave]](#manual-mleave)` are attempted in each verification condition.

Verification condition generation can be improved by defining appropriate [specification lemmas]](#manual---tech-term-Specification-lemmas) for a library.
The presence of good specification lemmas results in fewer generated verification conditions.
Additionally, ensuring that the [simp normal form]](#manual---tech-term-simp-normal-form) of terms is suitable for pattern matching, and that there are sufficient lemmas in the default simp set to reduce every possible term to that normal form, can lead to more conditionals and pattern matches being eliminated.

---



## The mvcgen tactic — 17.4. Enabling `mvcgen` For Monads {#manual-the-mvcgen-tactic-174-enabling-for-monads}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Enabling--mvcgen--For-Monads/

If a monad is implemented in terms of [monad transformers](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#--tech-term-monad-transformer) that are provided by the Lean standard library, such as `[ExceptT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#ExceptT)` and `[StateT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateT)`, then it should not require additional instances.
Other monads will require instances of `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)`, `[LawfulMonad](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Laws/#LawfulMonad___mk)`, and `[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk)`.
The tactic has been designed to support monads that model single-threaded control with state that might be interrupted; in other words, the effects that are present in ordinary imperative programming.
More exotic effects have not yet been investigated.

Once the basic instances are provided, the next step is to prove an [adequacy lemma]](#manual-mvcgen-adequacy).
This lemma should show that the weakest precondition for running the monadic computation and asserting a desired predicate is in fact sufficient to prove the predicate.

In addition to the definition of the monad, typical libraries provide a set of primitive operators.
Each of these should be provided with a [specification lemma]](#manual---tech-term-Specification-lemmas).
It may additionally be useful to make the internals of the state private, and export a carefully-designed set of assertion operators.

The specification lemmas for the library's primitive operators should ideally be precise specifications of the operators as predicate transformers.
While it's often easier to think in terms of how the operator transforms an input state into an output state, [verification condition]](#manual---tech-term-verification-conditions) generation will work more reliably when postconditions are completely free.
This allows automation to instantiate the postcondition with the exact precondition of the next statement, rather than needing to show an entailment.
In other words, specifications that specify the precondition as a function of the postcondition work better in practice than specifications that merely relate the pre- and postconditions.

**Example: Schematic Postconditions**

The function `[double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Postconditions_RPAR_)` doubles a natural number state:

```lean
def double : [StateM](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateM) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) [Unit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#Unit) := [do](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#Lean___Parser___Term___do)
[modify](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#modify) (2 * ·)
```

Thinking chronologically, a reasonable specification is that value of the output state is twice that of the input state.
This is expressed using a schematic variable that stands for the initial state:

```lean

⦃ fun s => ⌜s = n⌝ ⦄ [double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Postconditions_RPAR_) ⦃ ⇓ () s => ⌜s = 2 * n⌝ ⦄ := byn:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[fun]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) s [=>]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) n[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Postconditions_RPAR_) [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[PostCond.noThrow]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___noThrow) fun x s => [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 2 [*]](#manual-HMul___mk) n[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)
[simp]](#manual-simp) [[double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Postconditions_RPAR_)]n:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[fun]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) s [=>]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) n[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [modify](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#modify) fun x => 2 [*]](#manual-HMul___mk) x [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[PostCond.noThrow]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___noThrow) fun x s => [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 2 [*]](#manual-HMul___mk) n[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)
```

```lean

[simp]](#manual-simp) [[double]](#manual-double-_LPAR_in-Schematic-Postconditions_RPAR_)]Q:[PostCond]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond) [Unit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#Unit) ([PostShape.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) [PostShape.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure))⊢ [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[fun]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) s [=>]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) Q.[fst](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk) [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#Unit___unit)[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#Unit___unit) [(]](#manual-HMul___mk)2 [*]](#manual-HMul___mk) s[)]](#manual-HMul___mk)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [modify](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#modify) fun x => 2 [*]](#manual-HMul___mk) x [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)Q[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)
```
