The first projection of the postcondition is its stateful assertion.
Now, the precondition merely states that the postcondition should hold for double the initial state.

**Example: A Logging Monad**

The monad `[LogM]](#manual-LogM-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_)` maintains an append-only log during a computation:

```lean
structure LogM (β : Type u) (α : Type v) : Type (max u v) where
log : [Array](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Arrays/#Array___mk) β
value : α
instance : [Monad](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Monad___mk) ([LogM]](#manual-LogM-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) β) where
[pure](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Pure___mk) x := ⟨#[], x⟩
[bind](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Bind___mk) x f :=
let { [log]](#manual-LogM___log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_), [value]](#manual-LogM___value-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) } := f x.[value]](#manual-LogM___value-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_)
{ [log]](#manual-LogM___log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) := x.[log]](#manual-LogM___log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) ++ [log]](#manual-LogM___log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_), [value]](#manual-LogM___value-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) }
```

It has a `[LawfulMonad](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Laws/#LawfulMonad___mk)` instance as well.

The log can be written to using `[log]](#manual-log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_)`, and a value and the associated log can be computed using `[LogM.run]](#manual-LogM___run-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_)`.

```lean
def log (v : β) : [LogM]](#manual-LogM-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) β [Unit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#Unit) := { [log]](#manual-LogM___log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) := #[v], [value]](#manual-LogM___value-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) := () }
def LogM.run (x : [LogM]](#manual-LogM-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) β α) : α × [Array](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Arrays/#Array___mk) β := (x.[value]](#manual-LogM___value-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_), x.[log]](#manual-LogM___log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_))
```

Rather than writing it from scratch, the `[WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)` instance uses `[PredTrans.pushArg]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushArg)`.
This operator was designed to model state monads, but `[LogM]](#manual-LogM-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_)` can be seen as a state monad that can only append to the state.
This appending is visible in the body of the instance, where the initial state and the log that resulted from the action are appended:

```lean
instance : [WP]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk) ([LogM]](#manual-LogM-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) β) ([.arg]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure) ([Array](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Arrays/#Array___mk) β) [.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PostShape___pure)) where
[wp]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)
| { [log]](#manual-LogM___log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_), [value]](#manual-LogM___value-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) } =>
[PredTrans.pushArg]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pushArg) (fun s => [PredTrans.pure]](#manual-Std___Do___PredTrans___pure) ([value]](#manual-LogM___value-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_), s ++ [log]](#manual-LogM___log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_)))
```

The adequacy lemma has one important detail: the result of the weakest precondition transformation is applied to the empty array.
This is necessary because the logging computation has been modeled as an append-only state, so there must be some initial state.
Semantically, the empty array is the correct choice so as to not place items in a log that don't come from the program; technically, it must also be a value that commutes with the append operator on arrays.

Next, each operator in the library should be provided with a specification lemma.
There is only one: `[log]](#manual-log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_)`.
For new monads, these proofs must often break the abstraction boundaries of [Hoare triples]](#manual---tech-term-Hoare-triple) and weakest preconditions; the specifications that they provide can then be used abstractly by clients of the library.

```lean

⦃ fun s => ⌜s = s'⌝ ⦄ [log]](#manual-log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) x ⦃ ⇓ () s => ⌜s = s'.[push](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Arrays/#Array___push) x⌝ ⦄ := byβ:Types':[Array](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Arrays/#Array___mk) βx:β⊢ [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[fun]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) s [=>]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) s'[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple) [log]](#manual-log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) x [⦃]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)[PostCond.noThrow]](#manual-Std___Do___PostCond___noThrow) fun x_1 s => [⌜]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)s [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) s'.[push](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Arrays/#Array___push) x[⌝]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___pure)[⦄]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple)
[simp]](#manual-simp) [[log]](#manual-log-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_), [Triple]](#manual-Std___Do___Triple), [wp]](#manual-Std___Do___WP___mk)]All goals completed! 🐙
```

A function `[logUntil]](#manual-logUntil-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_)` that logs all the natural numbers up to some bound will always result in a log whose length is equal to its argument:

```lean
def logUntil (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : [LogM]](#manual-LogM-_LPAR_in-A-Logging-Monad_RPAR_) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) [Unit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#Unit) := [do](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#Lean___Parser___Term___do)
for i in 0...n do
```

## The mvcgen tactic — 17.5. Proof Mode {#manual-the-mvcgen-tactic-175-proof-mode}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The--mvcgen--tactic/Proof-Mode/

Stateful goals can be proven using a special *proof mode* in which goals are rendered with two contexts of hypotheses: the ordinary Lean context, which contains Lean variables, and a special stateful context, which contains assumptions about the monadic state.
In the proof mode, the goal is an `[SPred]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred)`, rather than a `Prop`, and the entire goal is equivalent to an entailment relation (`[SPred.entails]](#manual-Std___Do___SPred___entails)`) from the conjunction of the hypotheses to the conclusion.

syntaxProof Mode Goals

Proof mode goals are rendered as a series of named hypotheses, one per line, followed by [`⊢ₛ`]](#manual-Std___Tactic___Do___mgoalStx-next) and a goal.

```lean
[mgoalStx]](#manual-Std___Tactic___Do___mgoalStx-next) ::= ...
    | (ident : term)*
      ⊢ₛ term
```

In the proof mode, special tactics manipulate the stateful context.
These tactics are described in [their own section in the tactic reference]](#manual-tactic-ref-spred).

When working with concrete monads, `[mvcgen]](#manual-mvcgen)` typically does not result in stateful proof goals—they are simplified away.
However, monad-polymorphic theorems can lead to stateful goals remaining.

**Example: Stateful Proofs**

The function `[bump]](#manual-bump-_LPAR_in-Stateful-Proofs_RPAR_)` increments its state by the indicated amount and returns the resulting value.

```lean
[variable]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___variable) [[Monad](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/#Monad___mk) m] [[WPMonad]](#manual-Std___Do___WPMonad___mk) m ps]
def bump (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : [StateT](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#StateT) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) m [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) := [do](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Syntax/#Lean___Parser___Term___do)
[modifyThe](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Functors___-Monads-and--do--Notation/Varieties-of-Monads/#modifyThe) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) (· + n)

```
